`serialize_packet`: Serialize a `NetworkPacket` structure to a binary buffer. The `NetworkPacket` structure contains:
   - `packet_id`: uint32_t - packet identifier
   - `username`: std::string - user name (should be serialized with length prefix)
   - `scores`: std::vector<uint32_t> - a list of scores (should be serialized with length prefix followed by elements)
   - `metadata`: std::string - metadata string (null-terminated, use null_terminated adaptor)

1. `deserialize_packet`: Deserialize a binary buffer back to a `NetworkPacket` structure. The function should:

   - Read the username using the length prefix
   - Read the score count, then use read_container to read the scores vector
   - Read the metadata string as null-terminated for zero-copy
   - Skip any remaining padding bytes (if any)

2. `extract_packet_info`: Extract partial information from a serialized packet without fully deserializing it:
   - Use span() to get a zero-copy view of the packet_id (first 4 bytes)
   - Read username using prefixed adaptor to get a string_view
   - Skip the scores vector without reading its elements (read count, then skip the data)

`read_header_and_skip_body`: Read a message header from a binary buffer and skip the message body. The buffer format is:
   - `message_type`: uint16_t - message type identifier
   - `body_length`: uint32_t - length of the message body in bytes
   - `body_data`: variable length data (should be skipped)
   - `footer`: uint32_t - footer value

The function should:
   - Read the message_type
   - Read the body_length
   - Skip the body_data
   - Read the footer

Here is the code to finish the function, please output the complete contents of the file:

    uint16_t message_type;
    uint32_t body_length;

};

}

   - `item_count`: uint32_t - number of items
   - `items`: array of values (uint32_t or float depending on data_type)
